name: TLS handshake abstraction
benchmark_overlap_notes: Kept as TLS-family abstraction guidance for key schedule/transcript discipline; not the same protocol as benchmark KEMTLS.
complexity_notes: Medium-sized handshake model combining asymmetric setup, signatures, hashing, symmetric encryption, a transcript/key-derivation style structure, and compromise-aware security claims.
abstraction_lessons: Collapse concrete cipher-suite details into uninterpreted key schedule and transcript functions.
Keep transcript/check material in state facts so later Finished/authentication rules do not pattern-match huge histories.
Separate transport-key derivation events from terminal Commit events.
avoid_copying: Do not import record-layer-specific names into unrelated handshakes; reuse the phase/key-schedule abstraction only.

name: WireGuard compact DH handshake
benchmark_overlap_notes: Different real-world DH protocol; used for transcript/key-schedule abstraction only.
complexity_notes: A compact real-world DH protocol model with transcript hashes, derived chaining keys, identity binding, and a small number of terminal claims.
abstraction_lessons: Use transcript/chaining-key facts to summarize many prior messages instead of carrying full message tuples everywhere.
Place authentication events only after identity and transcript checks are represented in state.
Keep terminal secrecy/agreement lemmas focused on final transport keys and peer identity.
avoid_copying: Do not copy WireGuard-specific Noise pattern names; reuse the transcript-summary and terminal-claim placement.

name: 5G AKA fixed binding-channel model
benchmark_overlap_notes: No same-protocol AutoSM benchmark target in the current batch; retained for multi-role/stateful proof engineering principles.
complexity_notes: Large standard-derived model with stateful sequence numbers, multiple roles, resynchronization paths, source lemmas, custom heuristics, and scoped agreement claims.
abstraction_lessons: Split long standard text into phase-specific rules and separate agreement events per role pair and key material.
Use helper invariants for sequence-number/source reasoning before proving agreement.
Name role-pair and claim-kind inside Commit/Running payloads to avoid global injectivity explosions.
avoid_copying: Do not import 5G-specific SQN or SUPI details unless the target is actually a mobile-AKA protocol; reuse the phase split, helper invariants, and scoped agreement payload style.

name: RFID Feldhofer compact source-invariant model
benchmark_overlap_notes: Same broad RFID domain as benchmark LAK06 but different protocol; retained for source-invariant shape only.
complexity_notes: Small symmetric challenge-response model that uses a sources lemma to resolve partial deconstructions.
abstraction_lessons: When Tamarin leaves partial deconstructions, add a narrow sources lemma for the exact received constructor shape.
Use inequality or equality action facts for protocol checks instead of imperative conditionals.
Keep RFID challenge/response state facts small and role-local.
avoid_copying: Do not copy the Feldhofer protocol; transfer the partial-deconstruction repair shape.

name: SIV key-wrapping state/counter model
benchmark_overlap_notes: Different key-wrapping model; retained for handle/counter/source abstraction.
complexity_notes: Key-wrapping model with custom constructors, source-origin lemma, equality/inequality restrictions, counter uniqueness, monotonicity helper lemmas, and induction.
abstraction_lessons: For ticket/key-wrapping benchmarks, model handles, levels, counters, and tickets as separate fields rather than one giant opaque term.
Use origin/source lemmas for wrapped values and monotonicity restrictions for counters.
Place equality checks as Eq/NotEq action facts plus restrictions so rules stay declarative.
avoid_copying: Do not import SIV encryption equations unless the target explicitly needs a wrapping mode; reuse handle/counter/source abstraction.

name: Bluetooth LE pairing state-space control
benchmark_overlap_notes: Different standard protocol; retained for variant pruning and bounded-session discipline.
complexity_notes: Very large standard model with many pairing variants, DH consistency/validity restrictions, and deliberate one-session restrictions to prevent state explosion.
abstraction_lessons: For hard standard cases, choose one representative method/variant before codegen instead of modeling every branch.
Add OnlyOnce-style restrictions only when the benchmark asks for bounded representative runs.
Use Valid/Invalid point restrictions or Eq/NotEq checks for cryptographic validation rather than expanding validation algorithms.
avoid_copying: Do not inject Bluetooth-specific pairing variants into other protocols; transfer the variant-pruning and one-session-bounding discipline.

name: TPM envelope with reboot/loop proof support
benchmark_overlap_notes: Different platform protocol; retained for loop isolation and uniqueness-restriction principles.
complexity_notes: Stateful attestation/envelope model with restrictions, source typing, and comments about heuristic difficulty caused by looping state.
abstraction_lessons: When a reboot/reuse rule causes loops, isolate it behind state facts and prove typing/source helper lemmas first.
Use trace restrictions for challenge uniqueness and initialization uniqueness.
Keep attestation/signature verification as constructor-level checks, not imperative subroutines.
avoid_copying: Do not add TPM-specific PCR state to unrelated protocols; reuse the loop-isolation and uniqueness-restriction patterns.

name: Server-mediated symmetric ticket/key transport
benchmark_overlap_notes: Generic trusted-server ticket/key-transport abstraction guidance; intentionally avoids copying any benchmark-specific Needham-Schroeder, Denning-Sacco, or NSSK theory.
complexity_notes: Three-role symmetric protocols where a trusted server issues or transports a session key, an intermediate party may forward an encrypted ticket opaquely, and terminal agreement is established by challenge-response or key confirmation.
abstraction_lessons: Represent the server's session-key issuance as a compact origin event or state transition, then carry only the needed key, peer identities, and freshness values into terminal claims.
If an intermediate role receives a ticket encrypted for another party, thread and forward the opaque ciphertext rather than reconstructing it with a key that role should not know.
Use public message tags for each protocol message shape, but do not add new identity bindings, equality checks, or Lowe-style fixes unless the current protocol text requires them.
For injective agreement, place role/direction tags inside the canonical Commit/Running payload and tie uniqueness to a fresh challenge, ticket, or server-issued session-key witness.
Use OUT_/IN_ action facts and narrow [sources, reuse] lemmas as proof support only; do not add honest-source premises to attacker-facing receive rules.
avoid_copying: Do not copy a concrete five-message flow or benchmark lemma formula. Transfer only the ticket-forwarding, server-issue witness, tagged-message, and scoped-injectivity discipline.
